name: Chocolate-chip banana protein pancake bowls (baked)

source.author: Instagram (English, pasted text) — credited to @biteswithdina
source.notes: Baked 'pancake bowls': an egg + almond milk + 0% Greek yogurt + casein protein + flour batter with diced banana and chocolate chips, baked in two dishes at 350°F 20–25 min. The post's own macros per bowl: 505 kcal / 41 g protein / 58 g carb / 13 g fat. Independent estimate here: ~537 kcal / ~42 g protein / ~65 g carb / ~12.6 g fat — protein and fat match; carbs/calories run a little higher (banana size, flour scooping, and sugar-free syrup carbs). Casein taken as a typical ~110 kcal / 24 g protein scoop. Manual intake — reference only, not adopted. Estimate.

ingredients.note: whole-spelt flour is an easy swap
~200 kcal of the batch — the main lever

steps: Preheat to 350°F (175°C) and grease two oven-safe dishes.
Whisk the eggs, almond milk, yogurt, vanilla and sugar-free syrup.
Add the flour, protein powder and baking powder; mix until just combined.
Fold in the banana and half the chocolate chips.
Divide between the dishes, top with the remaining chips, and bake 20–25 min until golden and cooked through. Cool slightly.

batch_totals.note: Both bowls. Casein + Greek yogurt + eggs deliver the protein; chocolate chips (~200 kcal) and flour are most of the remaining calories.

him.verdict: A legitimately high-protein sweet breakfast — ~42 g protein per bowl (~7.8 g per 100 kcal) — that satisfies a dessert craving. It's a big portion though (~537 kcal, ~65 g carbs), and the ¼ cup of chocolate chips alone is ~100 kcal per bowl. Halve the chips and swap in whole-spelt flour and it becomes an 8.
flags: ~537 kcal / ~65 g carbs — a large breakfast
low fibre (~3.9 g) with white flour
suggested_mods: Halve the chocolate chips (−~50 kcal per bowl) — scatter them on top only, where you see/taste them
Add berries instead of half the banana for more fibre and vitamin C

her_preconception.verdict: Fine for her: eggs are fully baked (no raw-egg concern), yogurt is pasteurized, and it's a good protein + calcium + choline breakfast. Not a folate or iron source, and protein-powder choice matters in pregnancy — use a reputable, third-party-tested casein.

safety_advisories.note: Use a reputable, third-party-tested protein powder in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: a tested casein, or more Greek yogurt + an extra egg

suggested_mods: Add berries for vitamin C and fibre

cooking_guide: Whisk all the wet ingredients smooth first, then add the dry — casein clumps easily if it hits liquid unevenly.
Mix only until no dry streaks remain; overmixing makes protein bakes rubbery.
Casein batters are thick — that's normal; don't thin it out, it bakes up fluffy.
Dice the banana small so it's evenly spread and doesn't make wet pockets.
Check at 20 minutes: a toothpick in the centre should come out clean (melted chocolate aside). Overbaking dries protein-powder bakes fast.
Let them rest a few minutes — they finish setting as they cool.
